bullets.text: Q2 combined ratio was 92.6 with all products within profitability targets, accompanied by significant monthly variation. June catastrophe losses of $57 million, mostly hail, added to the quarter's $130 million catastrophe total.

Premium growth fell below expectations with early momentum waning. Commercial Lines experienced expected growth costs from corrective pricing, and special lines had low written premium growth partly from higher average premiums.

Direct auto new apps rose around 4% YOY with improving retention; Agency auto new apps trailed last year amid competitive pricing; Massachusetts Agency auto launched, achieving Direct-like Snapshot enrollment.

Year-over-year Direct auto policies in force increased around 7%, and Agency auto was flat, rounding from very slightly positive. Special lines policyholders grew about 1%, and multi-policy customer percentages continued growing.

Underlying severity trend estimates clustered around 3–4% for bodily injury and approximately 3–5% for physical damage, aligning with current pricing estimates amid sustained moderate consumer rate inflation.

Progressive-underwritten renters product announced for rollout over the next 18 months as a stepping stone to homeowners; Snapshot design changes enhanced attractiveness to independent agents and customers.

Multi-year policy processing system deployed across markets representing close to 80% of total premium, covering over half of active auto policies to facilitate essential real-time mobile capabilities.

Raised $350 million through 30-year Senior Notes at a 4.35% coupon, remaining well within debt-to-total capital guidelines. The investment portfolio realized modest year-over-year improvements in fully taxable equivalent total return.

Corrective pricing actions in Commercial Lines concluded, shifting focus to future growth; management emphasized matching future 3–5% severity trends across all products with smaller, inflation-aligned rate changes.

Second-quarter catastrophe losses totaled $130 million, with June hail losses of $57 million adding significantly. With the first hurricane already present, the company entered the third quarter well prepared for customers.
